history.content:
Please solve this issue: Wrong URL generated by get_admin_url for readonly field in custom Admin Site
Description
	
When a model containing a ForeignKey field is viewed (or edited) in a custom Admin Site, and that ForeignKey field is listed in readonly_fields, the url generated for the link is /admin/... instead of /custom-admin/....
This appears to be caused by the following line in django.contrib.admin.helpers get_admin_url:
url = reverse(url_name, args=[quote(remote_obj.pk)])
Other parts of the admin use the current_app keyword parameter to identify the correct current name of the Admin Site. (See django.contrib.admin.options.ModelAdmin response_add as just one example)
I have been able to correct this specific issue by replacing the above line with:
url = reverse(
	url_name,
	args=[quote(remote_obj.pk)],
	current_app=self.model_admin.admin_site.name
)
However, I don't know if there are any side effects and I have not yet run the full suite of tests on this. Mostly looking for feedback whether I'm on the right track.

history.content:
Please solve this issue: Wrong URL generated by get_admin_url for readonly field in custom Admin Site
Description
	
When a model containing a ForeignKey field is viewed (or edited) in a custom Admin Site, and that ForeignKey field is listed in readonly_fields, the url generated for the link is /admin/... instead of /custom-admin/....
This appears to be caused by the following line in django.contrib.admin.helpers get_admin_url:
url = reverse(url_name, args=[quote(remote_obj.pk)])
Other parts of the admin use the current_app keyword parameter to identify the correct current name of the Admin Site. (See django.contrib.admin.options.ModelAdmin response_add as just one example)
I have been able to correct this specific issue by replacing the above line with:
url = reverse(
	url_name,
	args=[quote(remote_obj.pk)],
	current_app=self.model_admin.admin_site.name
)
However, I don't know if there are any side effects and I have not yet run the full suite of tests on this. Mostly looking for feedback whether I'm on the right track.

history.content:
Please solve this issue: Wrong URL generated by get_admin_url for readonly field in custom Admin Site
Description
	
When a model containing a ForeignKey field is viewed (or edited) in a custom Admin Site, and that ForeignKey field is listed in readonly_fields, the url generated for the link is /admin/... instead of /custom-admin/....
This appears to be caused by the following line in django.contrib.admin.helpers get_admin_url:
url = reverse(url_name, args=[quote(remote_obj.pk)])
Other parts of the admin use the current_app keyword parameter to identify the correct current name of the Admin Site. (See django.contrib.admin.options.ModelAdmin response_add as just one example)
I have been able to correct this specific issue by replacing the above line with:
url = reverse(
	url_name,
	args=[quote(remote_obj.pk)],
	current_app=self.model_admin.admin_site.name
)
However, I don't know if there are any side effects and I have not yet run the full suite of tests on this. Mostly looking for feedback whether I'm on the right track.

history.content:
Please solve this issue: Wrong URL generated by get_admin_url for readonly field in custom Admin Site
Description
	
When a model containing a ForeignKey field is viewed (or edited) in a custom Admin Site, and that ForeignKey field is listed in readonly_fields, the url generated for the link is /admin/... instead of /custom-admin/....
This appears to be caused by the following line in django.contrib.admin.helpers get_admin_url:
url = reverse(url_name, args=[quote(remote_obj.pk)])
Other parts of the admin use the current_app keyword parameter to identify the correct current name of the Admin Site. (See django.contrib.admin.options.ModelAdmin response_add as just one example)
I have been able to correct this specific issue by replacing the above line with:
url = reverse(
	url_name,
	args=[quote(remote_obj.pk)],
	current_app=self.model_admin.admin_site.name
)
However, I don't know if there are any side effects and I have not yet run the full suite of tests on this. Mostly looking for feedback whether I'm on the right track.

history.content:
Please solve this issue: Wrong URL generated by get_admin_url for readonly field in custom Admin Site
Description
	
When a model containing a ForeignKey field is viewed (or edited) in a custom Admin Site, and that ForeignKey field is listed in readonly_fields, the url generated for the link is /admin/... instead of /custom-admin/....
This appears to be caused by the following line in django.contrib.admin.helpers get_admin_url:
url = reverse(url_name, args=[quote(remote_obj.pk)])
Other parts of the admin use the current_app keyword parameter to identify the correct current name of the Admin Site. (See django.contrib.admin.options.ModelAdmin response_add as just one example)
I have been able to correct this specific issue by replacing the above line with:
url = reverse(
	url_name,
	args=[quote(remote_obj.pk)],
	current_app=self.model_admin.admin_site.name
)
However, I don't know if there are any side effects and I have not yet run the full suite of tests on this. Mostly looking for feedback whether I'm on the right track.

Please solve this issue: Wrong URL generated by get_admin_url for readonly field in custom Admin Site
Description
	
When a model containing a ForeignKey field is viewed (or edited) in a custom Admin Site, and that ForeignKey field is listed in readonly_fields, the url generated for the link is /admin/... instead of /custom-admin/....
This appears to be caused by the following line in django.contrib.admin.helpers get_admin_url:
url = reverse(url_name, args=[quote(remote_obj.pk)])
Other parts of the admin use the current_app keyword parameter to identify the correct current name of the Admin Site. (See django.contrib.admin.options.ModelAdmin response_add as just one example)
I have been able to correct this specific issue by replacing the above line with:
url = reverse(
	url_name,
	args=[quote(remote_obj.pk)],
	current_app=self.model_admin.admin_site.name
)
However, I don't know if there are any side effects and I have not yet run the full suite of tests on this. Mostly looking for feedback whether I'm on the right track.

Please solve this issue: Wrong URL generated by get_admin_url for readonly field in custom Admin Site
Description
	
When a model containing a ForeignKey field is viewed (or edited) in a custom Admin Site, and that ForeignKey field is listed in readonly_fields, the url generated for the link is /admin/... instead of /custom-admin/....
This appears to be caused by the following line in django.contrib.admin.helpers get_admin_url:
url = reverse(url_name, args=[quote(remote_obj.pk)])
Other parts of the admin use the current_app keyword parameter to identify the correct current name of the Admin Site. (See django.contrib.admin.options.ModelAdmin response_add as just one example)
I have been able to correct this specific issue by replacing the above line with:
url = reverse(
	url_name,
	args=[quote(remote_obj.pk)],
	current_app=self.model_admin.admin_site.name
)
However, I don't know if there are any side effects and I have not yet run the full suite of tests on this. Mostly looking for feedback whether I'm on the right track.

Please solve this issue: Wrong URL generated by get_admin_url for readonly field in custom Admin Site
Description
	
When a model containing a ForeignKey field is viewed (or edited) in a custom Admin Site, and that ForeignKey field is listed in readonly_fields, the url generated for the link is /admin/... instead of /custom-admin/....
This appears to be caused by the following line in django.contrib.admin.helpers get_admin_url:
url = reverse(url_name, args=[quote(remote_obj.pk)])
Other parts of the admin use the current_app keyword parameter to identify the correct current name of the Admin Site. (See django.contrib.admin.options.ModelAdmin response_add as just one example)
I have been able to correct this specific issue by replacing the above line with:
url = reverse(
	url_name,
	args=[quote(remote_obj.pk)],
	current_app=self.model_admin.admin_site.name
)
However, I don't know if there are any side effects and I have not yet run the full suite of tests on this. Mostly looking for feedback whether I'm on the right track.

history.content:
Please solve this issue: Wrong URL generated by get_admin_url for readonly field in custom Admin Site
Description
	
When a model containing a ForeignKey field is viewed (or edited) in a custom Admin Site, and that ForeignKey field is listed in readonly_fields, the url generated for the link is /admin/... instead of /custom-admin/....
This appears to be caused by the following line in django.contrib.admin.helpers get_admin_url:
url = reverse(url_name, args=[quote(remote_obj.pk)])
Other parts of the admin use the current_app keyword parameter to identify the correct current name of the Admin Site. (See django.contrib.admin.options.ModelAdmin response_add as just one example)
I have been able to correct this specific issue by replacing the above line with:
url = reverse(
	url_name,
	args=[quote(remote_obj.pk)],
	current_app=self.model_admin.admin_site.name
)
However, I don't know if there are any side effects and I have not yet run the full suite of tests on this. Mostly looking for feedback whether I'm on the right track.

Please solve this issue: Wrong URL generated by get_admin_url for readonly field in custom Admin Site
Description
	
When a model containing a ForeignKey field is viewed (or edited) in a custom Admin Site, and that ForeignKey field is listed in readonly_fields, the url generated for the link is /admin/... instead of /custom-admin/....
This appears to be caused by the following line in django.contrib.admin.helpers get_admin_url:
url = reverse(url_name, args=[quote(remote_obj.pk)])
Other parts of the admin use the current_app keyword parameter to identify the correct current name of the Admin Site. (See django.contrib.admin.options.ModelAdmin response_add as just one example)
I have been able to correct this specific issue by replacing the above line with:
url = reverse(
	url_name,
	args=[quote(remote_obj.pk)],
	current_app=self.model_admin.admin_site.name
)
However, I don't know if there are any side effects and I have not yet run the full suite of tests on this. Mostly looking for feedback whether I'm on the right track.

history.content:
Please solve this issue: Wrong URL generated by get_admin_url for readonly field in custom Admin Site
Description
	
When a model containing a ForeignKey field is viewed (or edited) in a custom Admin Site, and that ForeignKey field is listed in readonly_fields, the url generated for the link is /admin/... instead of /custom-admin/....
This appears to be caused by the following line in django.contrib.admin.helpers get_admin_url:
url = reverse(url_name, args=[quote(remote_obj.pk)])
Other parts of the admin use the current_app keyword parameter to identify the correct current name of the Admin Site. (See django.contrib.admin.options.ModelAdmin response_add as just one example)
I have been able to correct this specific issue by replacing the above line with:
url = reverse(
	url_name,
	args=[quote(remote_obj.pk)],
	current_app=self.model_admin.admin_site.name
)
However, I don't know if there are any side effects and I have not yet run the full suite of tests on this. Mostly looking for feedback whether I'm on the right track.

class CustomAdminSiteReadonlyFkLinkTests(TestCase):
    @classmethod

    def test_readonly_fk_link_uses_custom_admin_site(self):

        section = Section.objects.create(name='Test section')

Please solve this issue: Wrong URL generated by get_admin_url for readonly field in custom Admin Site
Description
	
When a model containing a ForeignKey field is viewed (or edited) in a custom Admin Site, and that ForeignKey field is listed in readonly_fields, the url generated for the link is /admin/... instead of /custom-admin/....
This appears to be caused by the following line in django.contrib.admin.helpers get_admin_url:
url = reverse(url_name, args=[quote(remote_obj.pk)])
Other parts of the admin use the current_app keyword parameter to identify the correct current name of the Admin Site. (See django.contrib.admin.options.ModelAdmin response_add as just one example)
I have been able to correct this specific issue by replacing the above line with:
url = reverse(
	url_name,
	args=[quote(remote_obj.pk)],
	current_app=self.model_admin.admin_site.name
)
However, I don't know if there are any side effects and I have not yet run the full suite of tests on this. Mostly looking for feedback whether I'm on the right track.

class CustomAdminSiteReadonlyFkLinkTests(TestCase):

history.content:
Please solve this issue: Wrong URL generated by get_admin_url for readonly field in custom Admin Site
Description
	
When a model containing a ForeignKey field is viewed (or edited) in a custom Admin Site, and that ForeignKey field is listed in readonly_fields, the url generated for the link is /admin/... instead of /custom-admin/....
This appears to be caused by the following line in django.contrib.admin.helpers get_admin_url:
url = reverse(url_name, args=[quote(remote_obj.pk)])
Other parts of the admin use the current_app keyword parameter to identify the correct current name of the Admin Site. (See django.contrib.admin.options.ModelAdmin response_add as just one example)
I have been able to correct this specific issue by replacing the above line with:
url = reverse(
	url_name,
	args=[quote(remote_obj.pk)],
	current_app=self.model_admin.admin_site.name
)
However, I don't know if there are any side effects and I have not yet run the full suite of tests on this. Mostly looking for feedback whether I'm on the right track.

history.content:
Please solve this issue: Wrong URL generated by get_admin_url for readonly field in custom Admin Site
Description
	
When a model containing a ForeignKey field is viewed (or edited) in a custom Admin Site, and that ForeignKey field is listed in readonly_fields, the url generated for the link is /admin/... instead of /custom-admin/....
This appears to be caused by the following line in django.contrib.admin.helpers get_admin_url:
url = reverse(url_name, args=[quote(remote_obj.pk)])
Other parts of the admin use the current_app keyword parameter to identify the correct current name of the Admin Site. (See django.contrib.admin.options.ModelAdmin response_add as just one example)
I have been able to correct this specific issue by replacing the above line with:
url = reverse(
	url_name,
	args=[quote(remote_obj.pk)],
	current_app=self.model_admin.admin_site.name
)
However, I don't know if there are any side effects and I have not yet run the full suite of tests on this. Mostly looking for feedback whether I'm on the right track.

history.content:
Please solve this issue: Wrong URL generated by get_admin_url for readonly field in custom Admin Site
Description
	
When a model containing a ForeignKey field is viewed (or edited) in a custom Admin Site, and that ForeignKey field is listed in readonly_fields, the url generated for the link is /admin/... instead of /custom-admin/....
This appears to be caused by the following line in django.contrib.admin.helpers get_admin_url:
url = reverse(url_name, args=[quote(remote_obj.pk)])
Other parts of the admin use the current_app keyword parameter to identify the correct current name of the Admin Site. (See django.contrib.admin.options.ModelAdmin response_add as just one example)
I have been able to correct this specific issue by replacing the above line with:
url = reverse(
	url_name,
	args=[quote(remote_obj.pk)],
	current_app=self.model_admin.admin_site.name
)
However, I don't know if there are any side effects and I have not yet run the full suite of tests on this. Mostly looking for feedback whether I'm on the right track.

import datetime

class CustomAdminSiteReadonlyFkLinkTests(TestCase):
    @classmethod
    def setUpTestData(cls):
        cls.superuser = User.objects.create_superuser(

        from django.contrib import admin

        section = Section.objects.create(name='Test section')

            date=datetime.datetime(2009, 3, 18, 11, 54, 58), section=section,

            args=[section.pk],
            current_app='admin2',

        expected = reverse('admin:admin_views_section_change', args=[section.pk])
        self.assertIn(expected, html)

Please solve this issue: Wrong URL generated by get_admin_url for readonly field in custom Admin Site
Description
	
When a model containing a ForeignKey field is viewed (or edited) in a custom Admin Site, and that ForeignKey field is listed in readonly_fields, the url generated for the link is /admin/... instead of /custom-admin/....
This appears to be caused by the following line in django.contrib.admin.helpers get_admin_url:
url = reverse(url_name, args=[quote(remote_obj.pk)])
Other parts of the admin use the current_app keyword parameter to identify the correct current name of the Admin Site. (See django.contrib.admin.options.ModelAdmin response_add as just one example)
I have been able to correct this specific issue by replacing the above line with:
url = reverse(
	url_name,
	args=[quote(remote_obj.pk)],
	current_app=self.model_admin.admin_site.name
)
However, I don't know if there are any side effects and I have not yet run the full suite of tests on this. Mostly looking for feedback whether I'm on the right track.

import datetime

from django.contrib.admin.helpers import AdminReadonlyField
from django.contrib.auth.models import User
from django.test import TestCase
from django.urls import reverse

from . import customadmin
from .models import Article, Section


class CustomAdminSiteReadonlyFkLinkTests(TestCase):
    @classmethod
    def setUpTestData(cls):
        cls.superuser = User.objects.create_superuser(
            username='super', password='secret', email='super@example.com',
        )

    def setUp(self):
        self.client.force_login(self.superuser)

    def test_readonly_fk_link_uses_custom_admin_site(self):
        from django.contrib import admin

        section = Section.objects.create(name='Test section')
        Article.objects.create(
            title='a', content='c',
            date=datetime.datetime(2009, 3, 18, 11, 54, 58), section=section,
        )
        model_admin = admin.ModelAdmin(Article, customadmin.site)
        helper = AdminReadonlyField.__new__(AdminReadonlyField)
        helper.model_admin = model_admin
        remote_field = Article._meta.get_field('section').remote_field

        html = helper.get_admin_url(remote_field, section)
        expected = reverse(
            'admin:admin_views_section_change',
            args=[section.pk],
            current_app='admin2',
        )
        self.assertIn(expected, html)
        self.assertTrue(html.startswith('<a href="/admin2/'), html)

    def test_readonly_fk_link_uses_default_admin_site(self):
        from django.contrib import admin

        section = Section.objects.create(name='Test section')
        Article.objects.create(
            title='a', content='c',
            date=datetime.datetime(2009, 3, 18, 11, 54, 58), section=section,
        )
        model_admin = admin.ModelAdmin(Article, admin.site)
        helper = AdminReadonlyField.__new__(AdminReadonlyField)
        helper.model_admin = model_admin
        remote_field = Article._meta.get_field('section').remote_field

        html = helper.get_admin_url(remote_field, section)
        expected = reverse('admin:admin_views_section_change', args=[section.pk])
        self.assertIn(expected, html)
        self.assertTrue(html.startswith('<a href="/admin/'), html)

history.content:
Please solve this issue: Wrong URL generated by get_admin_url for readonly field in custom Admin Site
Description
	
When a model containing a ForeignKey field is viewed (or edited) in a custom Admin Site, and that ForeignKey field is listed in readonly_fields, the url generated for the link is /admin/... instead of /custom-admin/....
This appears to be caused by the following line in django.contrib.admin.helpers get_admin_url:
url = reverse(url_name, args=[quote(remote_obj.pk)])
Other parts of the admin use the current_app keyword parameter to identify the correct current name of the Admin Site. (See django.contrib.admin.options.ModelAdmin response_add as just one example)
I have been able to correct this specific issue by replacing the above line with:
url = reverse(
	url_name,
	args=[quote(remote_obj.pk)],
	current_app=self.model_admin.admin_site.name
)
However, I don't know if there are any side effects and I have not yet run the full suite of tests on this. Mostly looking for feedback whether I'm on the right track.

Please solve this issue: Wrong URL generated by get_admin_url for readonly field in custom Admin Site
Description
	
When a model containing a ForeignKey field is viewed (or edited) in a custom Admin Site, and that ForeignKey field is listed in readonly_fields, the url generated for the link is /admin/... instead of /custom-admin/....
This appears to be caused by the following line in django.contrib.admin.helpers get_admin_url:
url = reverse(url_name, args=[quote(remote_obj.pk)])
Other parts of the admin use the current_app keyword parameter to identify the correct current name of the Admin Site. (See django.contrib.admin.options.ModelAdmin response_add as just one example)
I have been able to correct this specific issue by replacing the above line with:
url = reverse(
	url_name,
	args=[quote(remote_obj.pk)],
	current_app=self.model_admin.admin_site.name
)
However, I don't know if there are any side effects and I have not yet run the full suite of tests on this. Mostly looking for feedback whether I'm on the right track.

import datetime

from django.urls import reverse

class CustomAdminSiteReadonlyFkLinkTests(TestCase):
    @classmethod
    def setUpTestData(cls):
        cls.superuser = User.objects.create_superuser(
            username='super', password='secret', email='super@example.com',
        )

    def setUp(self):

    def test_readonly_fk_link_uses_custom_admin_site(self):
        from django.contrib import admin

        section = Section.objects.create(name='Test section')
        Article.objects.create(
            title='a', content='c',
            date=datetime.datetime(2009, 3, 18, 11, 54, 58), section=section,
        )
        model_admin = admin.ModelAdmin(Article, customadmin.site)
        helper = AdminReadonlyField.__new__(AdminReadonlyField)

        remote_field = Article._meta.get_field('section').remote_field

            'admin:admin_views_section_change',
            args=[section.pk],
            current_app='admin2',
        )
        self.assertIn(expected, html)
        self.assertTrue(html.startswith('<a href="/admin2/'), html)

        from django.contrib import admin

        expected = reverse('admin:admin_views_section_change', args=[section.pk])
        self.assertIn(expected, html)

Please solve this issue: Wrong URL generated by get_admin_url for readonly field in custom Admin Site
Description
	
When a model containing a ForeignKey field is viewed (or edited) in a custom Admin Site, and that ForeignKey field is listed in readonly_fields, the url generated for the link is /admin/... instead of /custom-admin/....
This appears to be caused by the following line in django.contrib.admin.helpers get_admin_url:
url = reverse(url_name, args=[quote(remote_obj.pk)])
Other parts of the admin use the current_app keyword parameter to identify the correct current name of the Admin Site. (See django.contrib.admin.options.ModelAdmin response_add as just one example)
I have been able to correct this specific issue by replacing the above line with:
url = reverse(
	url_name,
	args=[quote(remote_obj.pk)],
	current_app=self.model_admin.admin_site.name
)
However, I don't know if there are any side effects and I have not yet run the full suite of tests on this. Mostly looking for feedback whether I'm on the right track.

import datetime

from django.contrib.admin.helpers import AdminReadonlyField
from django.contrib.auth.models import User
from django.test import TestCase
from django.urls import reverse

from . import customadmin
from .models import Article, Section


class CustomAdminSiteReadonlyFkLinkTests(TestCase):
    @classmethod
    def setUpTestData(cls):
        cls.superuser = User.objects.create_superuser(
            username='super', password='secret', email='super@example.com',
        )

    def setUp(self):
        self.client.force_login(self.superuser)

    def test_readonly_fk_link_uses_custom_admin_site(self):
        from django.contrib import admin

        section = Section.objects.create(name='Test section')
        Article.objects.create(
            title='a', content='c',
            date=datetime.datetime(2009, 3, 18, 11, 54, 58), section=section,
        )
        model_admin = admin.ModelAdmin(Article, customadmin.site)
        helper = AdminReadonlyField.__new__(AdminReadonlyField)
        helper.model_admin = model_admin
        remote_field = Article._meta.get_field('section').remote_field

        html = helper.get_admin_url(remote_field, section)
        expected = reverse(
            'admin:admin_views_section_change',
            args=[section.pk],
            current_app='admin2',
        )
        self.assertIn(expected, html)
        self.assertTrue(html.startswith('<a href="/admin2/'), html)

    def test_readonly_fk_link_uses_default_admin_site(self):
        from django.contrib import admin

        section = Section.objects.create(name='Test section')
        Article.objects.create(
            title='a', content='c',
            date=datetime.datetime(2009, 3, 18, 11, 54, 58), section=section,
        )
        model_admin = admin.ModelAdmin(Article, admin.site)
        helper = AdminReadonlyField.__new__(AdminReadonlyField)
        helper.model_admin = model_admin
        remote_field = Article._meta.get_field('section').remote_field

        html = helper.get_admin_url(remote_field, section)
        expected = reverse('admin:admin_views_section_change', args=[section.pk])
        self.assertIn(expected, html)
        self.assertTrue(html.startswith('<a href="/admin/'), html)

history.content:
Please solve this issue: Wrong URL generated by get_admin_url for readonly field in custom Admin Site
Description
	
When a model containing a ForeignKey field is viewed (or edited) in a custom Admin Site, and that ForeignKey field is listed in readonly_fields, the url generated for the link is /admin/... instead of /custom-admin/....
This appears to be caused by the following line in django.contrib.admin.helpers get_admin_url:
url = reverse(url_name, args=[quote(remote_obj.pk)])
Other parts of the admin use the current_app keyword parameter to identify the correct current name of the Admin Site. (See django.contrib.admin.options.ModelAdmin response_add as just one example)
I have been able to correct this specific issue by replacing the above line with:
url = reverse(
	url_name,
	args=[quote(remote_obj.pk)],
	current_app=self.model_admin.admin_site.name
)
However, I don't know if there are any side effects and I have not yet run the full suite of tests on this. Mostly looking for feedback whether I'm on the right track.
